voice: Mary speaks in a warm, clear and confident way, like a friendly product demo presenter, at a moderate pace with a natural rhythm. The recording is of very high quality, with the voice sounding clear and very close up.

lines.text: This is ForgePilot: a coding agent in VS Code, whose agent loop runs on TrueForge.
Task A. We select a function and ask for an inline edit.
TrueForge pauses the edit for approval, and it opens as a diff. Nothing is written until it is accepted.
In the terminal, debug set to off now reads as false. Then a single command undoes the change.
Task B. One request in agent mode, with no files named: add a flask config command that masks secrets.
First, ForgePilot builds a context pack within a fixed budget: keywords, ranked files, and the reason each was chosen.
From there, the agent explores on its own, through search and read tools that the extension serves over MCP.
Every edit arrives as a TrueForge tool approval, and is reviewed hunk by hunk in the diff editor.
It registers the new command, adds a test next to the existing ones, and documents it beside the other built-in commands.
When the free tier rate limits the model, ForgePilot backs off, then continues the same TrueForge session, without losing any progress.
Now we verify it. The command line tests pass, and flask config prints the settings as JSON.
Every secret, password, token and key is masked, and config appears in flask help.
lines.say: Every secret, password, token and key is masked, and the config command appears in flask help.

lines.text: And here is the same session, inside the TrueForge interface.
Cancel works mid-run. Here the agent is running the test suite. Cancel stops the TrueForge session and kills the command, so nothing is half-applied.
Task C. The first model has an invalid API key. It fails, and ForgePilot falls back to Gemini automatically.
The change is rejected in review, and git status stays clean. That's ForgePilot, from team FLOWSTATE.
